subject.title: PreparedModelCatalogConfigReplacedError poisons ingress spool and silences all agents when doctor --fix runs against a live gateway

question: Should `openclaw doctor --fix` fail clearly when a live gateway owns the configuration it may rewrite, or should OpenClaw support atomic live configuration replacement and prepared-state reload?
rationale: Both paths can address the report, but they create materially different public operational contracts and only source/runtime ownership review can establish whether a safe live-reload mechanism already exists.

options.title: Fail closed during live gateway operation
options.body: Detect the active gateway and refuse the repair with a clear stop–repair–start instruction; this is the recommended conservative recovery contract.

options.title: Support atomic live reload
options.body: Define a gateway lifecycle transaction that replaces configuration and prepared catalog state without dropping or poisoning in-flight dispatch.

recommendation.title: Fail closed during live gateway operation
recommendation.body: Detect the active gateway and refuse the repair with a clear stop–repair–start instruction; this is the recommended conservative recovery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter can clarify the observed deployment and reproduction while repository history is needed to identify the implementation owner.
